title: The eighth: Mina
hookLine: pilgrims go to Mina, a city of tents

lines: WHERE DID HE PRAY AT NOON?
cards: On the eighth day, where did the Prophet pray the noon prayer? Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay wanted a straight answer, so he asked Anas ibn Malik, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: tell me something you remember.
Anas answered: at Mina. The exchange is in Sahih al-Bukhari, and it's how the days of Hajj itself begin. Not at the Ka'ba.
Outside the city, in a valley of tents. Today, the eighth.

teach.h: THE FIRST DAY OF HAJJ PROPER.
teach.b: First, the date. The circling and the walking can be done at other times of year too. Hajj proper has its own days in the month of Dhul-Hijjah, and in Jabir's account they begin on the eighth, the day of tarwiyah.
Pilgrims who have come out of ihram enter it again, and the crowd moves out of Mecca to Mina. Second, what the Prophet did there.
Jabir's account in Sahih Muslim says that on that day they set out for Mina, and the Prophet prayed there the noon, afternoon, sunset, evening and dawn prayers.
Then he waited a little until the sun had risen, and went on.
That's the whole of the eighth: travel, five prayers, one night, and waiting. No great ritual. A pause before Arafah.
Third, the place now. Mina today is a valley filled with row after row of tents, white and fireproof, set up for the days of Hajj and almost empty the rest of the year.
People from far and wide sleep side by side on thin mattresses, share food, queue for the washrooms, and pray together on carpets laid over the ground.
The surgeon in white cloth from a week ago now shares a tent with strangers. Fourth, the end of Anas's answer.
He closed with a line: do as your leaders do. Pilgrims follow the group, move when it moves, rest when it rests.
The Qur'an, in surah two, speaks of the days spent here later in the Hajj; in Pickthall's words: "Remember Allah through the appointed days."
A city of tents is made for exactly that: not much to do, and plenty of time to remember.

how: On the eighth of Dhul-Hijjah, pilgrims enter ihram for Hajj if they are not already in it and go to Mina, where they pray the day's prayers, shortening those of four units, and spend the night before moving on to Arafah.

games.why: at Mina. then he adds: do as your leaders do. on Hajj, the group moves together.

practice: Sit somewhere snug, a corner of a room, the edge of a bed, a parked car, with nothing to do, and notice how close the walls are and how little you need.
If you pray, use the time for remembrance, a few words of praise you know, said slowly; if not, stay with the breath and the smallness of the space.
